title: Flower Planting With No Adjacent
summary: You manage n gardens, each with a unique label from 1 to n, and a network of bidirectional paths connecting them.
statement: You manage n gardens, each with a unique label from 1 to n, and a network of bidirectional paths connecting them. Each garden can be linked to at most three others. Your goal is to plant one of four flower types in each garden, ensuring no two directly connected gardens share the same flower type. Provide a valid planting plan as an array, where each element represents the flower type for the corresponding garden, with types numbered 1 through 4.
constraints: Each garden has degree at most three.
Use the smallest available flower type from 1..4 for gardens in label order.
hints: At most three neighbor colors can be forbidden when processing a garden.
Choose the smallest type 1..4 absent from already colored neighbors.
Build adjacency sets, then fill gardens in label order.
Four choices guarantee one remains, and later gardens will respect this color in turn.
editorial: Four choices guarantee one remains, and later gardens will respect this color in turn.

tests.explanation: Greedy assigns the triangle flower types one, two, and three.
Disconnected edges receive deterministic colors one,two,one,two.
